problem: Existing VLN benchmarks are split into discrete or continuous settings and treat humans as absent or static obstacles. HA-VLN 1.0 (HA3D) had misaligned motion data, discrete-only simulation, single-human scenes and coarse instructions.
motivation: Real-world deployment needs agents that respect personal space, ground instructions in human activities and re-plan under partial observability among moving crowds. A unified DE/CE benchmark with social metrics is needed for fair comparison and sim-to-real transfer.
key_idea: Build a unified discrete/continuous human-aware VLN benchmark (HAPS 2.0 multi-human motions, dual simulators, HA-R2R socially grounded instructions, collision-aware metrics, leaderboard) with baseline agents and real-robot validation.
insight: Explicit humans matter: replacing humans with cylinders reduces TCR by ~36% and raises SR, and models trained on R2R-CE drop 28.6% SR (CE) / 38.5% (DE) on HA-R2R validation, so humans are not generic obstacles. Training on HA-R2R keeps VLN-CE performance nearly unchanged (SR 0.35 vs 0.37). The step-size ablation shows larger steps reduce collisions only because collisions are checked at endpoints; checking every 0.25 m sub-step drives SR to ~0.
method: HAPS 2.0 dataset: 486 SMPL motions generated by MDM from verified region-grounded descriptions across 26 region types; 172 aligned motions after manual verification, 430+ annotation hours
Coarse-to-fine annotation: PSO places motions around objects (1 m safe distance, region bounds), then nine-camera multi-view manual refinement fixes mesh-object clipping
Multi-human enrichment: LLMs (ChatGPT-4, LLaMA-3-8B) propose multi-person scenes from nearby objects, four rounds of manual review, giving 910 humans in 428 regions of 90 scans
Dual simulators HA-VLN-DE/CE: dual-thread producer-consumer real-time human rendering (<50 ms), navmesh collision with revert, a unified API for human queries, scene updates and collision checks
HA-R2R: 16,844 R2R-CE instructions rewritten by LLMs to include human activities and social cues; test split of 3,408 instructions across 18 withheld buildings
Baseline agents: HA-VLN-VL (Recurrent VLN-BERT/PREVALENT, imitation learning) and HA-VLN-CMA (BERT + ResNet cross-modal attention + GRU, with EnvDrop and DAgger)
Metrics: TCR, CR, NE, SR (SR requires zero human collisions), plus a public leaderboard

setting.backbone: HA-VLN-VL (PREVALENT-init Transformer, fine-tuned), HA-VLN-CMA (BERT+ResNet-50+GRU, trained), BEVBert, ETPNav (retrained)
setting.training_data: HA-R2R (16,844 instructions) on HA-VLN-CE/DE; zero-shot variants trained on R2R-CE/VLN-CE only
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D in CE (90° FOV per view), panoramic RGB in DE
setting.action_space: CE: low-level forward 0.25 m / turn 15° / stop; DE: discrete viewpoint hops
setting.simulator: Habitat-based HA-VLN-CE and HA-VLN-DE (Matterport3D scans, 90 buildings)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT human info used only for collision metrics)

results: Human dynamics sharply cut performance: HA-VLN agents reach SR only ~0.09–0.14 on val-unseen and test, and BEVBert, the best baseline, gets SR 0.21 retrained on val-unseen. Training on HA-R2R improves SR over zero-shot transfer (BEVBert 0.15→0.21) without hurting VLN-CE. Real Go2 tests show NSR dropping with humans (HA-VLN-VL 0.44→0.18), with HA-VLN training better than VLN-CE (0.18 vs 0.12).
limitations: Own baseline agents are weak (SR ≤0.14) and are only reference implementations; BEVBert beats them
Humans follow pre-scripted 120-frame motions with short displacements, not reactive behavior; real-robot tests are small (30 episodes per setting) with collisions on sudden human moves
Instructions are LLM-generated and the SR definition requires zero collisions, coupling success to collision counting
